articles.title: Resident Evil Requiem is the best of both terrifying worlds
articles.summary: Capcom is releasing Resident Evil Requiem on February 27th on the PS5, Xbox, Switch 2, and PC, bringing together two different kinds of horror.
articles.body: Resident Evil has always been a strange creature: Like many of its most notable monsters, it has shifted and evolved into various forms. From its blocky days of tank-controlled Z-list actors to first-person fright fests, the franchise’s identity is not so much tied to genre as theme: zombies, viruses, very ugly monsters. Now, with Requiem, we have its first proper chimera, mixing the first-person horror of the latest installments with the fan-favorite action of Resident Evil 4. Along with this are two playable characters that embody these two very different styles, with beloved Leon S. Kennedy returning as a middle-aged action hero alongside newcomer Grace Ashcroft. The pair come together for a Resident Evil that seamlessly shifts between tone and view to create yet another terrifying evolution for the franchise. Requiem sees Grace, an FBI analyst, investigating a series of strange murders. All the victims are survivors of the 1998 Raccoon City Incident, the inciting event that’s central to much of Resident Evil’s history. Grace’s section begins in 2026 in a burnt-down hotel encased in a rainy urban environment, which reminded me of the cold, wet horror of David Fincher’s Seven. She navigates the dark hotel, armed only with a flashlight, before realizing she is not, in fact, alone. She soon finds herself in the hands of the main villain, Dr. Victor Gideon. [Image: The game lets you swap between first- and third-person views, but also recommends a particular view for each character. Much like the two previous entries, Biohazard and Village, Grace’s section is designed with a first-person viewpoint in mind. With her limited ammo and inventory space, low health, and tiny frame, Grace is this game’s unprepared horror protagonist, surrounded by enemies who can often kill her in one or two hits. Grace has to prioritize hiding, using one-off but powerful weapons and gadgets, and fleeing. Playing this in first-person helps articulate her vulnerability. Soon I was controlling Leon (who looks much worse for wear since his last appearance in Resident Evil 6, a game everyone, including me, pretends does not exist). Leon arrives near the hotel after Grace, and he’s soon killing zombies in the middle of a public street, giving chase to Gideon. It is rather unnerving watching Dr. Gideon shoot needles into innocent passersby as he escapes, quickly creating zombies. Leon’s sections are much like Resident Evil 4: third-person action, with melee prompts and a new ax weapon. Despite being in his 50s, Leon remains an efficient killing machine: As with his abilities in Resident Evil 4, Leon has melee and instant kills, with incredible animations and satisfying gore gushing from successful takedowns. There has never been this much gore caused by a Resident Evil protagonist; it’s glorious to watch him paint rooms red. It’s remarkable how seamlessly the game shifts between perspectives. If you have ever watched videos showing what first-person games look like from a third-person perspective, you will know things are… different. For example, when Grace opens a creepy cupboard, the game wants to show you a disgusting mass with ooze. The animation for her arms, the angle you view it from, and more will differ if you’re watching it from a first or third-person perspective. Incredibly, Requiem has achieved this fidelity for both angles at any time. It’s truly masterful work by Capcom. There is no optional character switching, however. You will simply find yourself playing Grace or Leon based on where you are in the story. For example, after playing as Grace for an hour, navigating very creepy hallways and avoiding a large monstrosity known only as the girl, she ends up being saved by Leon. The game then cuts back to show how Leon got the point of saving her. Later, when Grace is separated from Leon, you take over as Leon and give her covering fire from a sniper’s nest. You cannot predict when you will play as either character, but most of the first half of the game is in the shoes of Grace, with Leon’s sections notably shorter; by the time I crossed the halfway mark, the game put Grace on the back burner for a very long time. The mashup works surprisingly well, as it feels like the style of play reflects the characters and their particular story. Leon just could never be afraid, underprepared, or ill-suited to the horror around him by this stage in his story. Even with his bare hands, he is a formidable fighter, and remains the lovable weirdo from Resident Evil 4. His sections are refined, tight combat sequences; at one point you can even block a rocket with an ax. [Image: Grace is another story. Despite being an FBI analyst, she looks like a very small teenager. While I appreciate that her being unprepared adds to the horror, nothing portrayed her as a criminal analyst or FBI agent. Indeed, her being a lonely college student would have made more sense, as nothing in any part of the story demonstrated any abilities. Her backstory, which I won’t spoil here, is also underwhelming, and discovering why she is so important to the all-powerful villains left me rolling my eyes. While she felt good to play and embodied vulnerability, her constant sniveling and delivering lines with a whimper became very jarring. Thankfully she shows some growth toward the end of the game. The environments and scenarios are also wonderfully varied, throwing you from a creepy hospital-like area to the bombed-out remains of Raccoon City Police Department — also known as Leon’s origin story. It was quite emotional returning, as the original Resident Evil 2 was the first big-budget game I got in the 2000s. Leon and I were somewhat aligned in taking a breath before opening those doors. I chuckled as 50-year-old Leon commented on puzzles and items he dealt with nearly 30 years ago, which returning players will appreciate. The series’ enemies have also continued to evolve beyond just the shambling undead. My favorites were the new partially sentient zombies who retain some semblance of humanity — a cook keeps chopping decaying meat in the kitchen, a cleaner keeps rubbing a stained mirror and bashing her face, a hotel guest nursing a hangover keeps turning a light on and off. Grace can use these tics to her advantage when trying to escape them; for example, with the light-switcher zombie, you can turn on a light farther down a corridor to get him to move. Leon and Grace’s journey centers around what they believe is tracking down the last strain of the zombie virus that upended the world. I can safely say that the ending I got was one of the most satisfying conclusions to any Resident Evil game — and Requiem is a fitting name. This newest installment brings together two of the franchise’s heavy hitters — Resident Evil 4 and the first-person horror of Biohazard and Village — and at just under 11 hours, it doesn’t overstay its welcome, either. Over the years, Resident Evil has shown that it can be many different types of horror — and Requiem proves that the series can pull it all off in one single experience. Resident Evil Requiem launches on February 27th on the PS5, Xbox, Switch 2, and PC.

articles.title: Sara Ali Khan and Amrita Singh lease out 2,545 sq ft Mumbai office for Rs 3.76 crore over five years, with starting rent of Rs 5.85 lakh, deal includes 5% annual hike - Report
articles.summary: Sara Ali Khan and her mother, Amrita Singh, have leased a commercial office space in Mumbai’s Andheri West to artificial intelligence studio company
articles.body: Sara Ali Khan and her mother, Amrita Singh, have leased a commercial office space in Mumbai’s Andheri West to artificial intelligence studio company Upsurge Labs LLP for a five-year term. According to property registration documents reviewed by CRE Matrix, the deal has a total rental value of Rs 3.76 crore. The agreement includes an initial monthly rent of Rs 5.85 lakh, three car parking spaces and a 5% annual escalation.Sara Ali Khan and Amrita Singh’s Andheri West commercial property dealSara Ali Khan and Amrita Singh have rented out a 2,545 sq ft commercial office in the Signature building on Veera Desai Road, Andheri West, Mumbai. The property has a RERA carpet area of 2,545 sq ft and includes three car parking spaces. The leave and licence agreement was registered on September 29, 2026, for a period of 60 months. Upsurge Labs LLP, an AI studio company, is the tenant, with its partner Sowmay Jain representing the firm in the agreement.The five-year arrangement carries a total rental value of Rs 3.76 crore, as per the registration details reviewed by CRE Matrix.The agreement sets the initial monthly rent at Rs 5,85,350, while the security deposit stands at Rs 35,12,100. The lease commenced on October 1, 2026, with the tenant receiving a two-month rent-free period until November 30 to complete fit-out work. Rent payments are scheduled to begin on December 1, 2026. The agreement also provides for a 5% increase in rent every year over the five-year term.Based on the initial monthly rent and the stated carpet area, the rental rate works out to approximately Rs 230 per sq ft per month, before accounting for the annual escalation.No comment from Sara Ali Khan, Amrita Singh or Upsurge Labs yetThere has been no official response regarding the transaction from Sara Ali Khan and Amrita Singh.Saif Ali Khan’s commercial lease in Mumbai also made headlinesThe latest transaction follows news of a commercial property lease involving Sara Ali Khan’s father, actor Saif Ali Khan. According to CRE Matrix, Saif has leased two commercial units on Andheri Kurla Road, with a combined RERA carpet area of 5,692 sq ft. The agreement reportedly carries a monthly rent of Rs 22.76 lakh and was registered on September 29, 2026. The five-year lease covers the period from May 10, 2026, to May 9, 2031. The transaction adds to recent reports of commercial property activity involving members of the Khan family.Sara Ali Khan on work frontOn the professional front, Sara Ali Khan will be seen in 'Udta Teer', an upcoming Hindi spy action-comedy alongside Ayushmann Khurrana. Directed by Shashanka Ghosh, the film promises a blend of high-octane espionage and witty humor as the lead duo navigates an unexpected undercover mission. Originally slated to hit theaters on October 9, 2026, the makers pushed back the theatrical debut by two weeks. The spy entertainer is now scheduled to release in cinemas nationwide on October 23, 2026.Disclaimer: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: Arshad Warsi to return as original Jolly in ‘Jolly LLB 4’ after Akshay Kumar headlined second and third instalments with Umesh Shukla to direct prequel that will wrap filming by January 2027 - Report
articles.summary: Arshad Warsi is set to return as the quick-witted lawyer Jagdish Tyagi, popularly known as Jolly, in the anticipated fourth instalment of the 'Jolly LLB'
articles.body: Arshad Warsi is set to return as the quick-witted lawyer Jagdish Tyagi, popularly known as Jolly, in the anticipated fourth instalment of the 'Jolly LLB' franchise. According to a recent report, the upcoming film will be an exciting prequel directed by Umesh Shukla, with filming expected to wrap by January 2027. The makers are yet to finalise the official title. The development marks Warsi’s return to the main lead role after Akshay Kumar headlined the second and third films, bringing the franchise back to the character who started it all.‘Jolly LLB 4’ to be a prequel starring Arshad WarsiThe Jolly LLB franchise is preparing to return with a fourth film, with Arshad Warsi leading the project under the direction of Umesh Shukla. Variety India has reported that the film is in production and is expected to complete its shoot by January 2027. The title is yet to be finalised, while the project is currently in the final stages of pre-production.A source quoted in the report clarified that the upcoming film will revisit the franchise’s past rather than continue the story after the third instalment. “The project is currently in the last leg of pre-production. And it’s not taking the film forward. It’s a prequel,” the source said.The first three films were written and directed by Subhash Kapoor. Shukla, who has directed films such as OMG: Oh My God! and 102 Not Out, will now take charge of the fourth instalment. Details about the plot, the setting and the supporting cast have not yet been officially announced.Arshad Warsi returns as the original Jolly after Akshay Kumar’s two instalmentsWarsi first played Jagdish Tyagi, the small-town lawyer known as Jolly, in Subhash Kapoor’s Jolly LLB in 2013. The film built its appeal around a lawyer navigating the legal system, combining courtroom drama with humour and social commentary.Akshay Kumar subsequently took over the lead role in 'Jolly LLB 2' and returned for 'Jolly LLB 3' as Jagdishwar Mishra, another lawyer known as Jolly. The third film brought the two characters together for a courtroom face-off, giving the franchise an opportunity to pit its original protagonist against its newer central figure.With the fourth film reportedly planned as a prequel, Warsi will once again lead the franchise. The timeline also creates the possibility of revisiting the character’s earlier days, although the makers have yet to disclose how the story will unfold.Will familiar faces from the first ‘Jolly LLB’ return?The franchise has built a recognisable supporting ensemble around its courtroom stories. Saurabh Shukla’s judge, whose interventions have provided both comic relief and a moral counterpoint to the lawyers’ arguments, has been a recurring presence. His return to the fourth film has not been officially confirmed in the information available so far.The original 'Jolly LLB' also featured Amrita Rao, Boman Irani, Mohan Kapoor and Sanjay Mishra. Whether any of them will reprise their roles in the prequel remains to be seen. The makers are yet to announce the complete cast or reveal whether the new film will retain the earlier instalments’ familiar courtroom setting.What does Umesh Shukla bring to the ‘Jolly LLB’ franchise?Shukla has previously directed 'OMG: Oh My God!', a social satire built around questions of faith and accountability, and '102 Not Out', a character-driven comedy starring Amitabh Bachchan and Rishi Kapoor. His filmography spans humour and stories that use familiar social situations to explore broader themes.‘Jolly LLB 3’ box office performanceThe third instalment, directed by Subhash Kapoor and starring Akshay Kumar and Arshad Warsi, brought the franchise’s two lawyers together for a courtroom confrontation. According to Sacnilk’s box-office tracking, Jolly LLB 3 collected approximately Rs. 117.50 crore net in India, with India gross earnings of Rs. 140.14 crore and overseas collections of Rs. 31.50 crore. articles.title: Shashi Tharoor calls Ranveer Singh's 'Dhurandhar' a propaganda film: 'I think Pakistanis will realise how much wrong has been done in their name'
articles.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has shared his views on Aditya Dhar’s ‘Dhurandhar’ franchise after watching both instalments, which released in December 2025
articles.body: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has shared his views on Aditya Dhar’s ‘Dhurandhar’ franchise after watching both instalments, which released in December 2025 and March 2026, respectively. While the Ranveer Singh-led films have emerged as major commercial successes, they have also drawn mixed reactions, with some viewers accusing them of promoting propaganda. Tharoor acknowledged the political messaging in the films but praised their storytelling, plot twists and cinematic execution, describing the latter as “brilliant.”In a video shared on his official YouTube channel, Tharoor said he enjoyed the second instalment more than the first. “As a work of fiction, as a work of entertainment, there is no doubt that the second part is superb,” he said. However, he was critical of the graphic violence depicted in the films, calling it “totally excessive and over the top.”“There was no need to show so much violence, blood, mayhem, cruelty and some of the most disgusting scenes ever seen in Indian cinema,” he added.Addressing the criticism that ‘Dhurandhar’ promotes propaganda, Tharoor acknowledged that the films contain elements of political messaging. He also referred to reports of the films being banned in several countries, including Pakistan and some Gulf nations.“There is a lot of propaganda stuff built into it obviously and I gather the film has been banned in many countries, not just in Pakistan, but many of the Gulf countries have banned it, saying it would needlessly create bad blood between Indians and Pakistanis, so I can understand those feelings.”Tharoor also reflected on how audiences in Pakistan might respond to the films, saying, “I don’t know how Pakistanis will react if they see this. Some of the lines, I think Pakistanis will laugh. Some of the other things, I think Pakistanis will realise how much wrong has been done in their name.”Since the franchise revolves around an undercover intelligence operative, Tharoor also compared the film’s portrayal of intelligence work with his own interactions with officials in the field. While he said he had dealt with several intelligence personnel, his experience had been considerably different from the cloak-and-dagger operations depicted on screen.“I have dealt with a lot of our intelligence people but in a very civilised way, having analysis, conversations, information exchanges but not really getting into any cloak and dagger stuff. I am certainly not aware of commands being given that lead to explosions in faraway capitals. That’s not the world I have ever lived in,” he said.The Congress MP also discussed R Madhavan’s character in the films, which is loosely based on National Security Advisor Ajit Doval. Tharoor questioned the plausibility of one person remaining in the same position from the late 1990s to the present, pointing out that such continuity would be unlikely in a bureaucracy. However, he understood why the filmmakers might have chosen to retain the same character to carry the story forward.“I think it would be too much of a stretch to assume that’s true. So I would see this as a fictional film that tells a story which obviously is meant to impart a certain sense of lessons as well,” he said.Despite his reservations about the violence and political messaging, Tharoor had considerable praise for the franchise's filmmaking. He described both films as “vividly made” and said they were “bound to have an impact on anyone who has an imagination or a mind.” He also appreciated the “competent acting” and “superb sort of sets, design, direction.”Summing up his experience of watching the two films, Tharoor concluded, “At the end of 8 hours, you feel you have been through a major cinematic experience.”The ‘Dhurandhar’ franchise has collectively earned over Rs 3,100 crore worldwide. Alongside Ranveer Singh, the two films feature Akshaye Khanna, Arjun Rampal, Rakesh Bedi, Sanjay Dutt, Sara Arjun and R Madhavan in key roles.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2021, Reese Witherspoon sold a majority stake in Hello Sunshine at a $900 million valuation; five years later, she bought the company back
articles.summary: Reese Witherspoon has successfully bought back Hello Sunshine, her female-focused media company, at a fraction of its previous value. This follows her initial $900 million stake sale in 2021. Discover the journey and challenges faced by the company in the evolving media landscape.
articles.body: Reese Witherspoon, over the years, has started a lot of her own ventures, which also include her company Hello Sunshine. Starting at the rise of the streaming boom in the industry, she wanted to have a space for female creators in the industry to thrive and grow. Years later, in a deal to bring in more funds for the firm, she ended up selling the majority stake for a USD 900 million deal. Now, years later, after partnering with another media conglomerate, Witherspoon is back in the ownership circle, with almost 100% of the stake back under her name.Here is a look into the company’s overall journey.In 2016, Reese Witherspoon started her own companyReese Witherspoon and Seth Rodsky, along with backing from Peter Chernin and Jesse Jacobs' The Chernin Group, came up with an entirely new company called Hello Sunshine, which was built with the aim of championing female-driven stories and creators in the media realm that was heavily male-dominated.At the beginning of its establishment, the company acquired book rights via Reese's Book Club and produced hit television and film adaptations. These productions included ‘Big Little Lies,' ‘The Morning Show,' ‘Little Fires Everywhere,' ‘Daisy Jones & The Six,' and ‘Where the Crawdads Sing.'In August 2021, Reese Witherspoon sold off the majority of the stakes in her companyBBC reported that despite the ongoing success of her firm, Witherspoon’s company sold off the majority of its stakes for a lucrative deal at the time. A private equity-backed venture led by former Disney executives Kevin Mayer and Tom Staggs acquired a controlling majority stake in Hello Sunshine. The deal was settled for a whopping USD 900 million. Witherspoon netted an estimated USD 120 million in cash after taxes and retained an equity stake while staying on as a board member and producer.However, in the coming years, the overall valuation of independent productions dropped massively, and companies and platforms started pulling back on licensing budgets, third-party content spend, and overall production volume. Another major issue that dropped the overall valuation was the 2023 SAG-AFTRA and WGA strikes, which halted development pipelines across the industry. This, in turn, strained independent production entities even more, especially when most of them were dependent on overhead fees and greenlights.In October 2026, Reese Witherspoon bought back 100% of the companyOnly a few days ago, Variety reported that a European independent studio giant co-founded and led by CEO Pierre-Antoine Capton worked together with Reese Witherspoon to buy back her production company. The deal was estimated to be worth millions of dollars; however, the overall valuation is said to have been much less than what it was bought for earlier in 2021.Talking to The Wrap about the deal, the ‘Legally Blonde’ actress shared, “Mediawan has built a global, independent studio by putting creators first. That has always been my vision for Hello Sunshine. I'm investing alongside Mediawan and joining Pierre-Antoine Capton and his teams because this is the perfect home for this new media landscape.”While Witherspoon now has 100% under her name, the European conglomerate now also has access to all of the creative decisions that come under the firm’s future projects.DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: Hindus, Muslims celebrate festivals of both faiths in this Madurai village
articles.summary: Thenur near Madurai showcases Hindu-Muslim unity as Hindus offer seer varisai from Sundaravalli Amman temple for a renovated mosque inauguration.
articles.body: MADURAI: In a heartening display of communal harmony, Hindu residents of Thenur near Madurai brought traditional ceremonial offerings to mark the inauguration of a renovated mosque at the village, highlighting the spirit of unity and mutual respect among people of different faiths.The village, once known for the ban on the sale of alcohol and tobacco products, has now set an example of religious harmony. Hindu villagers offered ‘seer varisai’ (traditional gifts) consisting of Qurans, metal vessels, racks and a bureau for the madrassa, along with 10 varieties of fruits.P Sirajudeen, a villager, said the century-old Jumma Masjid in the village was reconstructed with contributions of around Rs 80 lakh from local villagers. The renovated mosque was inaugurated on Sunday and a community feast was organised as part of the celebrations, with nearly 3,000 people participating.“During the annual Purattasi (Tamil month) pongal festival at Sundaravalli Amman Temple in Thenur, Muslims actively participate. They contribute donations to the temple. When Hindu villagers abstain from consuming meat during the month, Muslims in the village follow the practice as well,” said S Karthigai Kumaran, another villager.Muslims also take part in the annual offering of the season’s first paddy harvest to Alagarkovil, an event held during the Tamil month of Thai. As part of the tradition, villagers collectively offer around 14 bags of paddy to the temple. “Muslims have offered their paddy harvest thrice so far,” he said.A Mohammed Riyaz said, “During the temple festival, members of the mosque offer special prayers when the idol of the temple goddess is brought and placed in front of the mosque, reflecting the long-standing communal harmony in the village. Muslims had not celebrated a major event for nearly 50 years, and the recent mosque inauguration was therefore a significant occasion for the community. Interestingly, the idol of the temple goddess was originally unearthed from a paddy field owned by the mosque.”Karthigai Kumaran said, “We decided to present a traditional seer varisai as a gesture of goodwill for the mosque’s inauguration. Men and women from the village took out a procession and offered the gifts to the mosque on Sunday.”When the procession reached the mosque, Jamaath members welcomed Hindu elders by draping shawls as a mark of respect and gratitude. articles.title: Dwayne Johnson Transforms Into a 70-Year-Old Man in Shocking ‘Lizard Music’ Set Photos
articles.summary: Move over, Mark Kerr, and make way for the Chicken Man. Dwayne Johnson was spotted in Brooklyn on Tuesday shooting his new movie “Lizard Music” from director...
articles.body:
Move over, Mark Kerr, and make way for the Chicken Man.

Dwayne Johnson was spotted in Brooklyn on Tuesday shooting his new movie "Lizard Music" from director Benny Safdie. Like with his previous collaboration with the "Uncut Gems" director, 2025's "The Smashing Machine," Johnson has gone through a serious prosthetic transformation. This time around, instead of a hulking MMA behemoth, Johnson has turned into a 70-year-old known as the Chicken Man.

In the set photos, Johnson, sporting a tan bucket hat and coat and holding a slice of pizza, walks alongside his young co-star Theo Clark Leber, who carries an oversized lizard plush. The artist behind Johnson's look is Kazu Hiro, who just turned Tom Cruise into a geriatric oil baron for "Digger."

"Lizard Music," based on Daniel Pinkwater's children's book of the same name, follows a young boy who "stumbles upon strange lizard musicians on late-night TV, leading him to befriend a peculiar man with an elderly chicken," according to an official logline. Other cast members include Rachel McAdams, Colman Domingo, David Krumholtz, Jeff Goldblum, Alicia Silverstone and Regina Hall.

From Amazon MGM Studios, "Lizard Music" is set for release on Christmas Day 2027.

During a career retrospective talk at the 2025 Toronto Film Festival, Johnson said it was an easy yes to sign on for "Lizard Music," sharing that it only took "about 45 minutes" of convincing from Safdie. He also revealed that he shed 30 pounds of muscle to play the Chicken Man.

"I'm so excited to get a chance to hopefully transform again like I was able to do in 'Smashing Machine,'" Johnson said . "[It means] eating less chicken."

articles.title: Roseanne Barr says Lisa Marie Presley gave her details about sleeping with Michael Jackson and Nicolas Cage
articles.summary: Barr said she believed the late daughter of Elvis Presley because she “never lied about s--- like that.”
articles.body:
Roseanne Barr says her friend Lisa Marie Presley, who died in 2023, gave her details about sleeping with Michael Jackson and Nicolas Cage.

Presley was married to Jackson in 1994. They split in 1996.

Cage and Presley wed in 2002 and broke up less than four months later.

Roseanne Barr claims that the late Lisa Marie Presley dished to her about the men in her life.

In Presley's case, that meant offering intimate details from her marriages to Michael Jackson and Nicolas Cage , both of whom the rocker was married to briefly.

"The best person that I ran around with was Lisa Marie Presley," Barr said in an interview published Tuesday in The Hollywood Reporter , after the former sitcom star was asked about having hung out with Madonna and Sandra Bernhard.

Barr said Presley, who died Jan. 12, 2023 at 54, had told her that Jackson was "the best lay she ever had."

When the interviewer challenged Barr, accusing her of lying, the actress stood by her story.

"No, I'm not [lying]," Barr replied. "She said he was the best lay and he had it going on. She said he told her all the things girls want to hear." He was "number one."

Jackson, who died June 25, 2009 at 50, married Presley in 1994 and they split two years later.

Barr, 73, said she believed Presley, too.

"She never lied about s--- like that," the former Roseanne star said. "She told me about Nicolas Cage and his business. She told me everybody she was with and their business, the size of it and the use and all of it."

Entertainment Weekly has reached out to a rep for Cage.

Presley, the only child of Elvis and Priscilla Presley, infamously married Elvis devotee Cage on Aug. 10, 2002. They split less than four months later.

Barr has been making the media rounds as she promotes her new, privately financed sitcom Meemaw: A Modern Day Fable , which costars Randy Quaid, Drea de Matteo, and Omar Gooding.

articles.title: Guitarrista do Offspring anuncia afastamento dos palcos por 'problema repentino e sério' de saúde | G1
articles.standfirst: Noodles publicou comunicado nas redes sociais da banda e informou que precisará pausar as apresentações ao vivo temporariamente. Segundo o post, a agenda da banda seguirá sem ele.
articles.summary: Noodles publicou comunicado nas redes sociais da banda e informou que precisará pausar as apresentações ao vivo temporariamente. Segundo o post, a agenda da banda seguirá sem ele.
articles.body:
Noodles, guitarrista da banda The Offspring, durante apresentação no Rock in Rio 2017 — Foto: Fábio Tito/G1

O guitarrista Noodles, integrante da banda de punk rock The Offspring, anunciou nesta quarta-feira (21) que precisará se afastar dos shows ao vivo em decorrência de um problema de saúde "bastante sério".

"É com profunda tristeza que tenho de anunciar que preciso me afastar das apresentações ao vivo por um tempo para lidar com um problema de saúde repentino e bastante sério", escreveu no texto, publicado nas redes do grupo.

"O resto da banda me dá cobertura, é super solidário e continuará agitando todos vocês na minha ausência. Espero voltar ao palco o mais rápido possível. Até lá, sentirei saudades de todos vocês com todo o meu coração. Obrigado por me manterem em seus pensamentos".

articles.title: D’Leesa, a cantora de 21 anos que viralizou fazendo tudo sozinha: 'Gravava no carro da minha mãe' | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista de 21 anos produz músicas e vídeos em casa, viralizou no TikTok e tem o Brasil como segundo maior país de ouvintes. Veja entrevista com o g1.
articles.summary: Artista de 21 anos produz músicas e vídeos em casa, viralizou no TikTok e tem o Brasil como segundo maior país de ouvintes. Veja entrevista com o g1.
articles.body:
D'Leesa no videoclipe de 'Hell or High Water' — Foto: Reprodução/YouTube

A cantora americana Cassidy D’Leesa Dzoole, conhecida como D'Leesa, é um fenômeno orgânico da internet como não se via há algum tempo.

Aos 21 anos, a artista de Atlanta, na Geórgia, faz tudo no estilo "do it yourself": é cantora, compositora, produtora, faz a mixagem e dirige os próprios videoclipes.

Sem grandes orçamentos ou produções, conquistou público em vários países — inclusive no Brasil, onde ela virá pela primeira vez para os festivais Batekoo (no dia 14 de novembro, em São Paulo) e No Ar Coquetel Molotov (no dia 28 de novembro, no Recife) .

Em entrevista ao g1 , por texto, D'Leesa contou que começou gravando os vocais no carro da mãe, usando o microfone dos fones de ouvido, e montava tudo no GarageBand. A artista conta que sempre gostou de compor, desde os 6 anos, mas parou na adolescência.

"Durante a adolescência, fui pressionada a seguir a carreira de STEM [Ciência, Tecnologia, Engenharia e Matemática], então parei de fazer música. Depois que me formei no ensino médio, em 2023, me senti com mais liberdade para explorar meus interesses", diz.

Só em 2025 ela comprou um microfone profissional. Foi também nesse ano que passou a usar as redes sociais para divulgar as músicas. "Eu filmava vídeos no meu quarto e postava no TikTok, no YouTube e no Instagram quase todo dia. Isso me ajudou muito a encontrar um público".

D'Leesa define o próprio estilo como "soul sáfico suave": músicas etéreas, às vezes dançantes, com letras sobre amar mulheres . Além de cuidar de todas as produções e vídeos, ela montou um site para divulgar o trabalho e vender produtos, como músicas personalizadas e itens de merchandising. "Tudo o que lanço atualmente é desenvolvido por mim", explica.

Esse estilo autêntico, "do it yourself", rapidamente atraiu fãs. Em outubro de 2025, D'Leesa postou no TikTok um vídeo cantando a música "Higher" e percebeu que o alcance disparava.

"Foi numa noite, em 2025. O vídeo estava ganhando milhares de visualizações e seguidores por minuto, e dias depois fui colocada na playlist Fresh Finds, do Spotify. Foi aí que pensei: 'Uau, as pessoas gostam das minhas músicas'", contou.

Em sua maioria, os vídeos de D'Leesa podem não ser grandes produções, mas são repletos de recursos: brincam com diferentes fundos, efeitos, sempre com a artista em evidência. Assim, ela chama a atenção não só por suas ótimas músicas, como pela forma dedicada e genuína que promove o próprio trabalho.

Um ano depois, D'Leesa revela que viver de música deixou de ser apenas um sonho.

"Chegou a um ponto em que a música é uma fonte real de renda para mim, e consegui sustentar partes da minha vida com streaming, vendas diretas, shows e outras oportunidades ligadas ao meu trabalho. Ainda estou transformando isso em algo totalmente sustentável a longo prazo, mas deixou de ser um sonho e virou algo tangível, que me sustenta financeiramente".

A vinda ao Brasil faz parte da primeira turnê da vida da artista. O público brasileiro é o segundo que mais consome a música de D'Leesa, de acordo com a cantora.

"Percebi que tinha fãs brasileiros quando chequei as estatísticas no Spotify for Artists e vi que o Brasil era meu segundo país com mais ouvintes. Acho que minhas redes sociais me permitem ter um público internacional, e sou muito grata por isso", disse.

Ela se apresenta no Brasil nos festivais No Ar Coquetel Molotov e Batekoo. Sobre a preparação para a estreia nos palcos, a cantora disse: "Essa é minha primeira turnê e estou muito animada para conhecer meus ouvintes. Estou me preparando fazendo exercícios e cantando ao mesmo tempo. Também ensaio o show como se estivesse no palco."

Perguntada sobre o que espera da passagem pelo Brasil, ela resume: "Espero uma festa: uma celebração da música, da expressão queer e do amor."

articles.title: Salman Khan was original target in shooting, Tiger Shroff an ‘easy second choice’ for Lawrence Bishnoi Gang: Reports
articles.summary: Actor Tiger Shroff was allegedly not the original target of the three shooters, who are reported to be members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.
articles.body: Actor Tiger Shroff was allegedly not the original target of the three shooters, who are reported to be members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. As per the latest reports, the shooters were reportedly targeting Bollywood superstar, Salman Khan, but allegedly abandoned their plans owing to the security arrangements at his residence.Salman Khan and not Tiger Shroff was original targetAccording to reports in various news publications, the three shooters involved in Sunday's firing incident in Mumbai's Juhu area had reportedly conducted a recce at Khan's home in Bandra. However, the security arrangements there reportedly discouraged them from carrying out the planned attack.On the look out for a comparatively easier target, the attackers allegedly monitored Tiger Shroff's movements through his Instagram account, as well as posts and videos shared by his fans, according to sources cited by IANS. The shooters reportedly watched the actor making his exit, before opening fire as his car.The incident took place on a busy Sunday evening and was captured on video. Tiger, the son of veteran actor Jackie Shroff, escaped relatively unhurt, however, his driver and a bystander sustained injuries.Accused arrested in RajasthanFollowing the firing, the accused reportedly fled to Surat in Gujarat before boarding a train to Jaipur. Their alleged plan was to travel to New Delhi by bus and then escape to Nepal. However, Mumbai Police arrested three accused in Rajasthan's Kota in connection with the case.Two of the arrested men have been identified as Ritik, alias Roshan, from Begusarai in Bihar, and Rehan from Sonipat in Haryana. Police have registered a case under charges of attempted murder and relevant provisions of the Arms Act.According to police sources, Rehan was in contact with Anil Pandit, an alleged associate of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. Following the incident, a social media post and an audio message from individuals claiming links to the gang surfaced, with the group allegedly claiming responsibility for the firing. The messages reportedly demanded an apology from Salman Khan to the Bishnoi community and threatened people associated with the actor.Salman Khan-Lawrence Bishnoi disputeThe long-running hostility between Salman Khan and Lawrence Bishnoi is linked to the 1998 blackbuck poaching case in Rajasthan. The Bishnoi community considers the blackbuck sacred, and Salman has faced repeated threats over the years, including a firing incident outside his Bandra residence in April 2024.Anup Jalota says apology could end hostilityMeanwhile, singer Anup Jalota has said that Salman Khan should apologise to the Bishnoi community to help bring an end to the ongoing hostility. Speaking to IANS, Jalota said, "I am very saddened by this. There is only one way to stop all this. Salman Khan should apologize to the Bishnoi community."He added, "I have said this before. It is very important that the Bishnoi community, which has been hurt, should be apologized to otherwise, the Bishnoi community will continue to be hurt. Those who work with Salman Khan will be hurt, their families will also be hurt."Jalota further urged Salman to take a firm decision to resolve the matter. "So, why not make a firm decision to apologize to the Bishnoi community to end this all? This is what I want."Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. The American rocker told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview that his political convictions have cost him corporate opportunities and late-night appearances, but he has no regrets about putting his beliefs first. Now, as he embraces a new chapter with his faith-inspired album, "Halfway 2 Jesus," the rocker says he's more concerned with sharing his message than winning back the entertainment industry. KID ROCK DETAILS SIT-DOWN WITH TRUMP, STEPHEN A. SMITH AND BILL MAHER Kid Rock, born Robert James Ritchie, has publicly supported President Donald Trump. He said the professional fallout has brought something he considers far more valuable — the freedom to speak his mind. "My relationship with Trump, yeah, that canceled all the, uh, any corporate deals coming my way. I don't really get invited to be part of, you know, things like the NFL or things like that … all the shows that I was so friendly with over the years, from all the late-night talk shows to my friend Jimmy Kimmel and Jimmy Fallon, I don't really get invited on there anymore," he said. "But who's to say that won't change … and I honestly, I don't care." The rocker said he expected to lose opportunities when he became more vocal about politics. "I put my country before pretty much everything except my family and God," he said. "So, yeah. There's been things like that, but that's no sweat off my back." WATCH: KID ROCK SAYS SUPPORTING TRUMP 'CANCELED ALL' CORPORATE DEALS AND LATE-NIGHT SHOW INVITES Kid Rock said he no longer has much patience for the corporate maneuvering that once came with his career, particularly when it meant worrying about how his opinions might affect his next opportunity. "I didn't enjoy the rat race of the music business. It was very necessary, and I'm glad I did it. And I'm thankful for all the opportunities that got me to where I am today," he said. "But the message I'm putting out now is so much more important than any of that." Kid Rock said he once felt pressure to watch what he said in the entertainment industry. Now, he enjoys speaking his mind without worrying about the professional consequences. "And years ago, when I went on this path to be more vocal and outspoken, I knew that stuff was going to go away. But man, let me tell you what freedom feels like," he said. KID ROCK TAPS EMINEM FOR CHRISTIAN ALBUM, PLANS BEER-AND-FAITH ARENA REVIVALS "To be able to speak your mind anywhere, anytime and really exercise … the freedom of speech that so many brave souls died for, to be able to express that, when I want and how I want and not have to worry about anything in between." "No radio station. No corporate deal or show or anything, you know … it's just the biggest, most awesome feeling of freedom that one could ever imagine," he said. Kid Rock's next move isn't about winning back Hollywood. It's about faith, forgiveness and a rock 'n' roll revival. WATCH: KID ROCK ADMITS EMINEM CRITICIZING TRUMP TESTED THEIR FRIENDSHIP The rocker said his new album, "Halfway 2 Jesus," blends Christian themes with high-energy rock and features a collaboration with his friend of nearly 40 years, Eminem, who has publicly criticized Trump. The "Cowboy" singer told Fox News Digital that Eminem's public criticism of Trump had tested their relationship, particularly after the rapper criticized the president in a performance at the 2017 BET Hip Hop Awards. "There's been moments when, yeah, friendships have been tested. With Eminem, it would probably be, you know, when he did the thing at the BET Awards, where he's just going hard in the paint against Trump," Kid Rock said. Kid Rock said he ultimately respected his longtime friend's right to express his views despite their political differences. "But you know what I mean? At the end of the day, I looked at it like, man, that's his truth. That's how he feels," he said. "I genuinely don't like people talking about my friends in a bad way, and I'm very quick to defend them, family and friends. But when you're in the political arena, that’s a whole different ballgame," he said. WATCH: KID ROCK CREDITS ERIKA KIRK'S FORGIVENESS OF HUSBAND'S ACCUSED ASSASSIN WITH TRANSFORMING HIS FAITH For Kid Rock, the Eminem collaboration carries a message beyond music. In the foreword to "Halfway 2 Jesus," he said he hopes their friendship serves as an example for people whose political differences have strained personal relationships. "We hope that sets an example for people who've lost friends or stopped talking to family because they think differently." The rocker said he attended Kirk's memorial with his son and was moved by Kirk's widow, Erika, who publicly forgave the man accused of killing her husband. articles.title: Adult Film Star Blames Dating Apps and Social Media Fir Gen Z’s Sex Recession: ‘P*rn Is The Least Of It’
articles.summary: Gen Z is commonly said to be facing a “sex recession,” but adult film actress Alix Lynx disagrees with the claim that adult film is the main culprit in young...
articles.body:
Gen Z is commonly said to be facing a "sex recession," but adult film actress Alix Lynx disagrees with the claim that adult film is the main culprit in young people's decreasing rate of having sex.

According to a study conducted by the Kinsey Institute of Indiana University, young adults today engage in a very small amount of sexual activity despite being very sexually driven. As part of the survey of 2,373 Americans aged 18 to 29, 29% reported not having any sexual partners in the last three months, and 19% have never had one. Playboy and the birth control brand Julie sponsored and supported the study.

Thirty-seven-year-old Lynx has worked in the adult industry for 14 years. A native of New York City, she holds a bachelor's degree in broadcast journalism and an MBA in digital marketing. Lynx quit her corporate job to become an adult film star, according to her contributor bio on The Daily Beast.

Though Lynx admits adult film does have complications around intimacy between a couple, she says the problem goes deeper than that.

"Honestly, I think p*rn is the least of it," Lynx says. "P*rn has always existed. I think social media and dating apps are much bigger factors."

Lynx thinks constant screen time has replaced many things that used to bring people together.

"I think social media has completely changed our lives," she says. "We're on the internet all the time, staying home instead of going out and actually living our lives. We're not expanding our horizons, meeting new people or having new experiences. You end up living your life through the lens of a screen."

"I think that has a lot to do with why people are having less sex and dating less," Lynx continues. "You can't replace real human interaction, energy, and connection with social media or the internet."

"If you actually want to date and meet people," Lynx says, "At some point you have to get off your phone and meet someone in person."

She believes dating apps have worsened the situation by giving singles the illusion of an endless number of matches.

"Dating apps give you this endless supply of people," she said. "You can scroll and scroll, match and match, and that alone becomes a dopamine hit."

"Instead of thinking, 'I matched with this person, I like them, let's meet in real life,' people become pen pals and then swipe again to see what's next because there could always be someone better."

Many young app users feel the same way. According to a Forbes Health survey of 1,000 U.S. dating app users in 2024, conducted by OnePoll, 76% experienced burnout on dating apps in the past year, while Gen Z users are more likely to say they always feel this way.

Lynx thinks that the same mentality applies to social media, which offers another attractive person right around the corner.

"You can find someone hot, slide into their DMs and start talking, but then another hot person appears and suddenly your attention is somewhere else," she said. "We're in this era where everyone is constantly asking, 'What's next? What's the next best thing?' You could spend your entire life searching for what's next."

At the same time, researchers study whether digital life has replaced some physical connections.

According to the Kinsey study, 25% of young adults reported that online interactions, such as messaging, social media, or AI companions, fulfilled some of their intimacy or emotional needs. In contrast, 28% said time spent on screens or online activities decreased their motivation to form a physical connection with someone.

The researchers concluded that the main problem seems to be a lack of opportunity rather than a lack of desire. 74% of survey participants said that they have moderate to strong sexual desire, but 42% claimed that having sex is not a priority for them right now. In addition to dating exhaustion, fear of rejection, and financial worries, the institute named changing social norms. 43% of participants said that financial struggles make it harder to date and maintain relationships.

However, the shift toward digital connection is also evident in the adult-content world. According to OnlyFans discovery platform OnlySearch, there were 7.3 million searches made in 2026, with "couple" and "wife" being among the top 20 most searched phrases. Also, creators whose bios mentioned such terms as "girlfriend experience" or "girl next door" got more clicks, which means that fans might be looking for intimacy in addition to sexual content.

However, Lynx is sure that overuse of screens will lead to communication problems in the future.

"People are so used to living through a screen that when it comes to interacting in person, it's almost like 'use it or lose it,'" she said. "You can become socially awkward because you don't actually have to talk to people anymore, and I think that's become an issue."

"You miss so much through a screen," she said. "You miss tone, nuance, somebody's energy, and what they're actually like in person. Online you can just not respond for two days, but in real life you actually have to communicate."

Though she doesn't put pornography at the center of the problem, Lynx agrees that her industry might also be partly to blame. Being available to anyone instantly makes it harder to have intimacy in real life, when people try to imitate what they have seen in pornography scenes.

"I definitely think p*rn could be making real-life intimacy harder for some people," she said.

"I've hooked up with guys in the past who have pulled moves on me that I know they've seen in my scenes," Lynx says. "I'm sitting there thinking, 'You've watched my scenes before because that's something I do when I'm performing, not something I typically do in real life.'"

"That creates a real disconnect because p*rn is entertainment," she noted. "It's not necessarily a representation of what sex is actually like."

According to the Kinsey survey, p*rn fills a gap for some young people. As reported by Fast Company, 34% of young men said that p*rn completely satisfies their sexual desires, and one in three people who put a high priority on sex said that they chose digital or solo sex over having sex with a partner.

However, Lynx emphasizes that the main change is not the existence of p*rn, but its accessibility everywhere.

"The difference now is that p*rn is so accessible," she said. "People have it at their fingertips all the time, and that creates issues we haven't really had to navigate before."

"If your partner is at home but you're constantly on your phone watching p*rn instead of going to them for intimacy, then yeah, that can really interfere with things. It becomes this quick fix rather than actually connecting with your partner."

In her neighborhood, New York City ranked second on the list of OnlySearch users, with nearly 29,000 active users during the year ending in September.

From her experience of online work, Lynx regularly sees how easy it is to replace something that would normally help to build a connection with the partner via digital sexual interaction.

"I talk to a lot of guys through my texting apps who are at work or sitting in the office," she explained. "Instead of texting their significant other and saying, 'I can't wait to see you later,' they can pull out their phone and get that instant gratification. That can replace a moment where they could have been building anticipation and connection with their partner."

The results of the Kinsey survey go along with a longer trend. According to an analysis of the General Social Survey done by the Institute for Family Studies, the percentage of Americans aged 18 to 29 who reported no sex in the past year doubled from 12% in 2010 to 24% in 2024. In addition, young adults spent only 5.1 hours a week with friends in 2024, compared with 12.8 hours in 2010. Time spent on smartphones, social media, pornography, and video games is among the reasons for this.

However, there is no consensus on how deep the slump is. The Kinsey survey didn't compare Gen Z to previous generations, and only 18% of respondents said that they were unsatisfied with their sex lives. And half of the young adults surveyed don't even think that there is a sex recession.

For Lynx, it goes way beyond pornography. She is convinced that a generation of people who used to get entertainment, attention, and possible partners at the touch of a button is gradually losing what can't be achieved online: real human connection.

articles.title: Spotify is busting free of CarPlay with the launch of its first native car app
articles.summary: Spotify launched its next-gen, fully native in-car app built on Google’s Android Automotive OS. The standalone app launches today in select Audi models.
articles.body: Spotify announced Wednesday the launch of its next-generation, fully native in-car app, built directly on Google’s Android Automotive operating system. The standalone app, which is launching today in select Audi models, runs directly on the vehicle’s infotainment hardware — eliminating the need for phone tethering, Bluetooth connections, or aux cables. It’s the clearest sign yet that Spotify is ready to move beyond Apple CarPlay and Android, popular phone projection systems that currently dominate the way most people consume media in their cars. And with 34 percent of Spotify’s monthly active users and 77 percent of Premium subscribers streaming music in their cars, the platform they use to listen has never been more important. Spotify’s new native app will launch with several Audi models, including the electric A6 e-tron and Q6 e-tron, as well as the gas-powered A5, Q5, and A6. Jonathan Tarlton, Spotify’s automotive business development lead, said the app, which has been in development for a little more than a year, is about delivering a more inviting experience to users — and specifically one that’s completely controlled by Spotify. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Spotify’s standard Android Automotive app operated as a “headless” integration, meaning that Spotify supplied the underlying backend data, playlists, and music catalog, but Google’s templates dictated how the interface was drawn and structured onscreen. The new Audi application is “headful,” allowing Spotify to draw and render its own native UI directly on the vehicle’s screens from scratch. “We’re drawing all the pixels,” Tarlton said in an interview. “We own the user experience. So we’re not in a template or a framework. It’s 100 percent Spotify.” To be sure, Spotify isn’t turning its back on Apple CarPlay and Android Auto; the company is still “heavily invested” in phone projection, Tarlton assured us. That said, the native Spotify app is being set up to compete directly with phone mirroring. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto remain the default way many people listen to music or podcasts in their vehicles: Drivers get in, connect their phones automatically, and tap into their familiar mobile interface. A native Spotify app could encourage people to listen through the car’s own operating system instead of projecting their phones — a scenario that Tarlton says he welcomes. "“We’re drawing all the pixels. We own the user experience. So we’re not in a template or a framework. It’s 100 percent Spotify.”" - Jonathan Tarlton, head of automotive business development at Spotify “We want to give users choice,” he said. “We want to be wherever they are and we want to make sure that they’re accessing Spotify in the way they want to access it, whether they’re locked into the iOS ecosystem … or Android on the phone as well.” People may love their CarPlay, but the experience is not without its tradeoffs. Wireless connection, in particular, can be spotty depending on your vehicle. Tarlton said the new app is aimed at reducing some of those headaches, like “a cold start in the morning,” he said. “You’re not having to wait to boot. You’re not having to wait for a screen to load. You’re not having to plug your phone in.” There are other benefits to using the native Spotify app over a projected one from your phone. Passengers can scan a QR code displayed on the screen to join a wireless “Spotify Jam” session and add songs directly to the queue from their smartphones. On vehicles with a dedicated secondary passenger display, front passengers can browse, view lyrics, and watch video content without disturbing the driver. And while the vehicle is parked or charging, those motion graphics, like video podcasts and lyrics, move to the central display so everyone can enjoy. With these features in particular, Spotify feels like it’s doing its part in helping to bring car passengers together again, Tarlton said. Often today you’ll find parents rocking out to their favorite hits in the front while kids are wearing their headphones in the back. The new app aims to correct that dynamic. “I’m excited that we can bring joy to the cabin again,” he said. “It’s not just technology.” The rollout of the new Spotify app will focus in particular on cars with Android-based operating systems, he said. In that way, Spotifty can avoid having to build separate, bespoke applications for every individual automaker. Rather, the company can use a standard Android Automotive APK that it can then distribute through multiple app stores, whether it’s the Google Play Store or proprietary automaker stores like the Audi Application Store. “Our number one goal was to prevent fragmentation, not just for our sake, but for the sake of the whole industry,” Tarlton said, “because we believe in having an open and fair place for apps to play — and the car is such a great place for that.”

articles.title: Del universo Marvel a rescatar al héroe olvidado del Everest
articles.standfirst: Tom Hiddleston es Edmund Hillary en 'Tenzing', la película que reivindica el papel Tenzing Norgay en la primera ascensión al Everest.
articles.summary: Tom Hiddleston es Edmund Hillary en 'Tenzing', la película que reivindica el papel Tenzing Norgay en la primera ascensión al Everest.
articles.body: Tom Hiddleston, conocido entre otros papeles por el papel de Loki en el universo Marvel, se ha puesto en la piel de Edmund Hillary en la película 'Tenzing', que se puede ver en Apple TV. Dirigido por Jennifer Peedom, el filme reivindica la figura del sherpa Tenzing Norgay, el hombre que acompañó a Hillary en la primera ascensión confirmada al Everest, el 29 de mayo de 1953. Una gesta grabada en la historia del alpinismo, pero cuyo relato tradicional concedió durante décadas un mayor protagonismo al montañero neozelandés que a su compañero sherpa. Esta versión cinematográfica recorre la vida de Norgay, encarnado por Genden Phuntsok, desde sus primeros años en el Himalaya hasta alcanzar la cima del techo del mundo. El reparto incluye a Willem Dafoe, que interpreta al coronel John Hunt, responsable de la expedición británica, y a Caitríona Balfe, en el papel de Jill Henderson, secretaria de la expedición y aliada de Tenzing. También tiene un rol destacado Thinley Lhamo, que da vida a Dawa, la esposa de Tenzing, cuyo apoyo resulta para que su marido fuera miembro oficial de la cordada. Antes de llegar a la cima junto a Hillary, el sherpa ya había participado en seis expediciones al Everest. En 1952, alcanzó junto al alpinista Raymond Lambert una altitud aproximada de 8.595 metros, la mayor altitud alcanzada hasta la fecha. La cima se le resistió entonces, pero aquella experiencia confirmó su extraordinaria capacidad para desenvolverse en las condiciones extremas de la montaña. Un año después regresó con la expedición dirigida por Hunt, dispuesto a culminar el sueño que perseguía desde hacía años. Mientras Phuntsok creció en la meseta tibetana entre yaks y caballos, para Hiddleston todo era un descubrimiento durante el rodaje. Como parte de la preparación para su papel, el actor completó una expedición hasta el campamento base del Everest. "Fue una idea de la directora. Quería que experimentáramos el paisaje por nosotros mismos, que sintiéramos la belleza y la maravilla del valle de Khumbu. Vimos el Everest juntos por primera vez, al mismo tiempo", recuerda Hiddleston. Tras ese recorrido, el rodaje arrancó en Katmandú y después se trasladó a Nueva Zelanda, donde se filmaron las escenas de gran altitud. Un grupo de alpinistas expertos asesoró a los actores y al equipo técnico. Entre ellos estaba Guy Cotter, que ha coronado seis veces el Everest. Hiddleston y Phuntsok tuvieron que escalar en hielo y enfrentarse a situaciones que exigían una preparación física y técnica específica. El actor británico llegó incluso a caer en una grieta durante una de estas experiencias y quedó sujeto por la cuerda que Phuntsok llevaba asegurada a la cintura, un episodio que recordó uno de los peligros reales a los que se enfrentaron Hillary y Tenzing. La película no se limita a recrear las dificultades físicas de aquella expedición. También aborda las diferencias culturales y sociales que separaban a los alpinistas occidentales de los sherpas, cuyo conocimiento del Himalaya resultaba esencial para avanzar por sus laderas. Mientras muchos montañeros europeos concebían el Everest como una cumbre que conquistar, para Tenzing tenía además una dimensión espiritual. Esa diferencia de perspectivas constituye uno de los ejes del relato, que presenta la ascensión como una empresa colectiva basada en la confianza y el respeto mutuo. Peedom, documentalista y cineasta especializada en el mundo de la montaña, quiso rodar esta película para poner en valor la figura de Tenzing, tantas veces relegada a un segundo plano cuando se habla de la primera conquista del Everest. Su experiencia previa en el Himalaya le permitió acercarse a una historia que va más allá de la hazaña deportiva y que también habla de identidad y tradición. Con 'Tenzing', Peedom propone poner en el lugar que corresponde al sherpa en aquella gesta y recordar que detrás de esta primera ascensión al Everest hubo dos protagonistas unidos por una misma cuerda y un objetivo compartido.

articles.body: Actor Renuka Shahane has expressed concern over the firing incident linked to Tiger Shroff, describing it as a “very scary thing” and saying she was relieved that the actor was safe. Calling for firm action against those responsible, she stressed that such acts of violence must be addressed at their source to prevent them from recurring. The incident, which took place in Mumbai’s Juhu area, has raised concerns about the safety of people associated with the film industry.Renuka Shahane says Tiger Shroff is ‘safe and sound’ after firing incidentSpeaking to IANS, Renuka Shahane expressed relief that Tiger Shroff had escaped unharmed, while highlighting the fear such incidents can create. “This is a very scary thing. And thank God, Tiger Shroff is safe and sound. But this terror is very scary. Nothing like this has happened in the industry for many years. We are seeing it now, and I think everyone should be very careful about this. Otherwise, no one will come out of the house. Everyone will leave with security,” she said.The actor also pointed to the uncertainty surrounding the motives of those who carry out such acts, particularly when firearms are involved. She said the incident could leave people feeling vulnerable and questioning their safety.“I think everyone will be scared because the people who do such things are so mad. We do not understand what they want or what they want to do, and they have weapons in their hands. So, this is a scary thing,” Renuka added.Renuka Shahane urges authorities to tackle the problem ‘from the roots’Calling for decisive action, Renuka said that such incidents must be addressed at their source rather than allowed to create an atmosphere of fear. Emphasising the need to prevent similar incidents in the future, she said, “But I think everyone knows that this should be destroyed from the roots. Otherwise, nothing will happen.”Her remarks come amid concerns about the safety of actors and others working in the entertainment industry following the firing incident.Tiger Shroff firing incident: What happened in Juhu?The firing took place on October 18 outside a football club near Pushpa Narsee Park in Mumbai’s Juhu area. Tiger Shroff was not injured in the incident, while his driver and an autorickshaw driver were reportedly hurt.According to reports, three suspects were subsequently apprehended in Kota, Rajasthan, in connection with the case. articles.title: Tyler Cameron reveals he’s having a baby with fiancée Tate Madden during ‘DWTS’ dedication night routine
articles.summary: This just might be a “Dancing With the Stars” first!
articles.body: This just might be a “Dancing With the Stars” first! During his Dedication Night performance on Oct. 20, Tyler Cameron revealed that he and fiancée Tate Madden are expecting their first child together. The moment happened as he danced a contemporary alongside partner Sharna Burgess dedicated to his late mom. During rehearsals, he got emotional saying that weddings make him super emotional because he won’t be able to dance with his mom at his. He then reflected on marrying Madden soon. While dancing to “Supermarket Flowers” by Ed Sheeran, voiceover of Cameron reading a letter to his mom was heard. During one moment, he revealed that he is going to be a father. “You would’ve loved the woman I’m gonna marry ... she’s going to be the most incredible momma, just like you,” he said. “And we’re going to have a baby. I can’t believe I’m going to be a dad. Wish you were here. Hope that I make you proud.” Madden joined Cameron on the dance floor and they cradled her baby bump as the news was announced. As they ended their dance, Alfonso Ribeiro did a gender reveal and pink confetti exploded in the ballroom. “It’s a girl!” Alfonso Ribeiro announced, as he asked the couple how they were feeling. “This is incredible. I get to be a girl dad, what a gift,” Cameron said. “I get to be her husband soon and the father of our beautiful baby.” The judges were emotional after the performance and reveal, with Bruno Tonioli saying, “You were dancing with three hearts, beating as one.”

articles.body: Was he unwell or just drunk? The questions on veteran singer Daler Mehndi being publicly upbraided by a minister during a show in Uttarakhand for a sub-par performance abound with many in the industry rallying behind him and at least one fellow artiste saying the audience deserved better.Actor Anupam Kher, stand-up comedian Vir Das and singers Shaan, Palash Sen, Gurdas Maan and Alisha Chinai were among those who said that Mehndi, who has three decades of singing behind him, is unwell, does not drink and should have been accorded more respect.Singer Sona Mohapatra, however, said a veteran should get "dignity, empathy and gratitude for a lifetime of contribution". The audience, she added, also deserves "an honest performance, or at the very least, an honest acknowledgement when that is no longer possible".On Sunday evening, the 59-year-old singer of hits such as "Tunak Tunak Tun", "Bolo Ta Ra" and "Ho Jayegi Balle Balle" was performing at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in Uttarakhand's New Tehri town when state minister Subodh Uniyal stormed up to the stage and asked him loudly if he was drunk.Mehndi, dressed in his trademark ornate sherwani and bejewelled turban, considerably thinner than his previous public appearances and barely moving on stage, can be heard saying "sorry" in video clips that have since gone viral.It was a rare instance of an artist of such repute being called out mid-performance by organisers."Couple of days ago, I saw a video in which Daler Mehndi ji was singing on stage and some minister got up and spoke to him insultingly. I wasn't there so I don't know but I've known Daler ji for 25 to 30 years. I know that he does not drink and he is one of the finest human beings that I have met. I personally know that he has not been keeping well for two-three years," Kher said in a video on X on Wednesday."Nobody should speak to anybody like this and that also on a public forum. This is not fair. To publicly accuse someone like this is wrong. Daler ji I am so sorry," he said.Comedian Vir Das said his first international show was in Dubai for Mehndi's show."So not just music people, comedy people also have a lot to owe to this great man and this great artist. And he was humble, nice, supportive and amazing. Daler paaji, I hope you feel well in your corner. Thank you from a very young comedian," Das said on Instagram.Comedian-actor Rajpal Yadav, who starred alongside Mehndi in the recently-released movie "Welcome To The Jungle", released a video on Instagram, saying the minister should not have used "inauspicious words" for a person whose "voice has served the country and the world for decades"."Minister ji, this does not suit you. It seems as if you have bought art. Art can never be bought. Art is life, so respect life. And for your information, Daler paaji does not drink. I have also worked with him in 'Welcome to the Jungle'. He has not been keeping well. And everyone is trying to make him better," he said.Mehndi's brother, singer Mika Singh, on Tuesday confirmed that the artiste had undergone a major surgery and challenged anyone to prove that his elder brother ever touched alcohol.Though there has been speculation about Mehndi's health, the nature of his illness and surgery is not clear.Support for the singer has been pouring in, particularly after Mika backed his brother and took on detractors as well as the minister.Commenting on Mika's post, Shaan said, "Daler Paaji is the Original Rockstar!!!! He has shown the World how to Rock n Roar!!!"Maan, the popular Punjabi singer known for hit tracks such as "Dil Da Mamla Hai", "Challa" and "Ki Banu Duniya Da", shared a note on his Instagram Stories, describing Mehndi as an "iconic artist who has given so much to our music"."He has undergone a surgery and hasn't been keeping well. His recent performances also reflect that. Yet, he chose to honour his commitment to his fans."Every person deserves dignity, compassion and respect. Mehndi Saab, jeeyonde raho. Waheguru sabh nu chardi kala vich rakhe. (May you live long, Mehndi Saab. May Waheguru keep everyone in high spirits and bless them with strength and prosperity)," he said.Jassi, another Punjabi singer popular for "Dil Le Gayee", "Kudi Kudi", "Nishani Pyar Di" and "Laung Da Lashkara", backed Mehndi on his Instagram Stories."Daler bhajiii Sharab nai Peende bhraaaa (Brother Daler doesn't drink alcohol, bro!)"Chinai, the voice behind popular 1990s and 2000s tracks "Made in India", "Tinka Tinka" and "Kajra Re", said no one had the right to come on stage and insult Mehndi."Daler Mehndi Rocked your world with his Powerful n Infectious Music !!! He doesn't need to prove he can sing to anyone or seek any Validation... We all use Backing tracks n Minus one tracks on our Shows !! How dare anyone come onstage n insult him in this Manner !!!! It Speaks of Tasteless Behaviour n Reflects poorly of the Minister on the contrary !!! Daler paji we all love you," she said.Sen hailed Mehndi as a "legend, a pioneer, and the King of Bhangra" who brought joy and unforgettable music to millions across the globe."They see memes and headlines.. I see a man who has given his entire life, sweat, and soul to spreading happiness, uplifting culture, and serving through his art and philanthropy," he said on Instagram."Even legends can fall ill, but can't disappoint their fans by not showing up. You showed up and tried to do your best. People may mock, criticize, or judge, but no amount of noise can erase your legacy, your kindness, or the unshakeable dignity with which you carry yourself," he added.Mohapatra took a centrist approach to the controversy, recalling a past performance of Mehndi, which she said, was underwhelming."If someone is unwell, there must be compassion and a responsible way to handle the situation. What cannot become acceptable is for audiences and organisers to repeatedly bear the consequences while everyone around the artist looks away."I don't know whether the minister in Uttarakhand handled the situation appropriately. That is a separate question. But does the manner of his objection automatically invalidate the substance of the complaint? I ask this as a fellow performing artist, fully aware that I may be criticised for saying it," she wrote.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Mick Jagger y cómo fue cambiando su estilo de vida: "Después de cierta edad, ya no se puede abusar del alcohol y las drogas"
articles.standfirst: El artista explica su estilo de vida a los 83 años
articles.summary: El artista explica su estilo de vida a los 83 años
articles.body: El cantante, compositor y líder de la banda 'The Rolling Stones', Mick Jagger, se sinceraba a sus 83 años, en el programa 'Sunday Sitdown'. Su extensa carrera le ha llevado a viajar por todo el mundo y a disfrutar de muchísimas experiencias. Una vida plena y en lo profesional. El artista contaba lo que hace a diario para estar preparado para moverse y andar kilómetros durante sus shows. De hecho, ya puntualizó a 'GQ' que su entrenamiento "es un poco como el tenis. Te mueves muy rápido y luego paras. Y luego caminas. De alta intensidad. Como dices, siempre estás en movimiento". Ahora bien lo que no soporta son los baños de hielo. "Son horribles. No creo que sea una moda que vaya a durar. A veces me preocupa que sea algo pasajero". Es más, sobre sus rutinas añadía que hay que mantenerse "con vida y en forma. Hay un límite a lo que puedes hacer… Quiero decir, desearías que hubiera algo nuevo que pudieras probar, pero ¿realmente hay algo? No hay nada realmente… Quiero decir, hay un montón de cosas que están por venir de las que siempre lees, ¿y luego llegan alguna vez? Mientras tanto, estás en el gimnasio, mientras tanto, estás en el estudio de baile". "Después de cierta edad, ya no se puede abusar del alcohol y las drogas. Es muy divertido, pero si quieres mantenerte en forma y vivir muchos años, no puedes consumir drogas ni beber alcohol constantemente. Yo lo dejé cuando tenía 40 años", señalaba el artista dejando evidente que cuando el tiempo pasa hay que extremar las situaciones.

articles.title: Andrew Shue and Marilee Fiebig —Amy Robach and T.J. Holmes’ exes —are engaged after 3 years together
articles.summary: “I don’t know how it happened, but there’s a happy ending.”
articles.body:
Andrew Shue confirmed that he proposed to Marilee Fiebig earlier this year.

The Melrose Place star and the lawyer connected as their former spouses, Amy Robach and T.J. Holmes, made headlines for their romantic relationship.

"We're very grateful and hopeful," Shue told PEOPLE.

Andrew Shue has confirmed his engagement to Marilee Fiebig.

"We're very grateful and hopeful," the Melrose Place alum told Entertainment Weekly's sister site PEOPLE in an interview published on Wednesday. "I don't know how it happened, but there's a happy ending."

Shue and Fiebig famously got together months after their respective exes —and former GMA3 coanchors —Amy Robach and T.J. Holmes became romantically involved. Robach and Holmes made headlines in November 2022 when they were photographed cozying up. The news anchors later claimed they were separated from their spouses at the time. Robach and Shue finalized their divorce in March 2023 while Holmes and Fiebig's marriage officially ended in October 2023. (Robach and Holmes got married last month .)

"I had to accept my own part in marriage not working out for me and in not understanding myself well enough and not understanding what matters in a relationship well enough to find the right person for me, and that has been an extraordinary gift," Shue told PEOPLE. "Again, I don't know how it happened, but I can say I'm grateful."

He added: "I had to grow through a lot of pain and a lot of struggle and a lot of humility. I think the magic of love is when you go from a need to giving."

The actor confirmed on Wednesday that he had proposed to Fiebig earlier this year. The engagement came after Shue launched his The Forum nonprofit , "a virtual town hall to bring people together to create the renewal agenda" in January.

"It's one thing to work on projects that you think can help people and change the world," he explained. "The most important project is your family and building a foundation for your kids and creating a home and showing them a loving relationship they can see and experience."

Shue is the father of three sons: Nate, 30, Aidan, 28, and Wyatt, 23, with ex-wife Jennifer Hageney. Fiebig, meanwhile, shares daughter Sabine, 13, with Holmes.

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

When discussing how he and Fiebig got together, Shue said "it just happened." The actor referred to it as "freak luck" that they were able to get together romantically. "This just happened to be a circumstance that allowed for that," he continued. "I don't think there was anything other than this just happened to be our way of getting to know each other and being able to share ourselves with each other in a time where we both needed a friend."

He went on to compare the "equilibrium" going on in his life right now to what's happening in America. "We've been through a lot and we're ready to balance it out, but it's only going to happen through collective action and if we turn back towards each other."
