articles.title: Arijit Singh's concert package in Mumbai goes up to Rs 11.8 lakh which accommodates 15 people, Diljit Dosanjh's top ticket costs Rs 18,000 - Details inside
articles.summary: Arijit Singh and Diljit Dosanjh are gearing up for major India tours, but fans hoping to catch the singers live will face a stark difference in ticket
articles.body: Arijit Singh and Diljit Dosanjh are gearing up for major India tours, but fans hoping to catch the singers live will face a stark difference in ticket prices. While Arijit’s most expensive concert package is priced at Rs 11.8 lakh, Diljit’s top ticket costs Rs 18,000. Both artists are set to begin their respective tours at Ahmedabad’s Narendra Modi Stadium, although their approaches to concert pricing differ considerably.Arijit has announced a nine-city India tour in 2027 to celebrate 20 years in the music industry. The concerts are expected to feature some of his biggest hits, including ‘Agar Tum Saath Ho’, ‘Tum Hi Ho’ and ‘Vida Karo’. The announcement comes months after the singer revealed in January that he would step away from playback singing to focus on his independent musical pursuits.Scheduled to run from January to May 2027, the tour will offer tickets across a wide price range. Entry-level tickets for the Ahmedabad concert at Narendra Modi Stadium start at Rs 999, while the most expensive package, available at Mumbai’s Mahalaxmi Racecourse, costs Rs 11.8 lakh for a table accommodating 15 people.According to thumpN, the tour’s official ticketing partner, premium packages across cities are priced between Rs 7 lakh and Rs 10 lakh. Designed for groups seeking a more exclusive experience, these packages include couch seating, special gifts, premium alcohol bottles, dedicated entry and exit points, and separate lavatories.The luxury experience also extends to social media. Guests will have a dedicated content creator film an Instagram Reel featuring them at the concert, with the video shared the following day. Despite the steep prices, demand for the premium categories remains strong, with reports suggesting that around 60% of the top-priced options have already been sold. Arijit has witnessed similar demand in the past, with a 40-seater premium lounge at his Pune concert reportedly selling for Rs 16 lakh three years ago.The singer’s 2027 tour is expected to draw around five lakh people across nine cities. Ahmedabad will host the opening concert on January 9, followed by Chandigarh on January 23 and Jaipur on February 7. The tour will then move to Mumbai on February 20, Bengaluru on March 13 and New Delhi on March 27. Pune is scheduled for April 10, followed by Indore on May 1 and Hyderabad on May 15.Diljit Dosanjh, meanwhile, is preparing for the India leg of his ongoing Aura World Tour. Following the success of his 2024 Dil-Luminati Tour, which reportedly generated Rs 943 crore in revenue, the Punjabi singer is set to perform in several Indian cities. Unlike Arijit’s premium hospitality offerings, Diljit’s highest-priced tickets for the upcoming shows are capped at Rs 18,000, making the concert experience comparatively more accessible to fans.Diljit has been performing across Europe and North America as part of the Aura World Tour this year. The India leg will begin in Delhi-NCR on November 1, followed by Indore on November 15, Ahmedabad on November 21, Mumbai on November 27 and Bengaluru on November 29. He will then perform in Lucknow on December 5. A Chandigarh show has also been announced, although the promoter is yet to share further details.Arijit Singh first rose to prominence after participating in the reality show ‘Fame Gurukul’ in 2005. Over the years, he has become one of Hindi cinema’s most popular playback singers, delivering chartbusters such as ‘Gerua’, ‘Channa Mereya’, ‘Ae Dil Hai Mushkil’, ‘Bulleya’, ‘Naina’, ‘Zaalima’, ‘Galti Se Mistake’, ‘Ae Watan’, ‘Mast Magan’, ‘Rait Zara Si’, ‘Kesariya’, ‘Apna Bana Le’, ‘Jhoome Jo Pathaan’, ‘Tum Kya Mile’, ‘Ve Kamleya’, ‘Chaleya’, ‘Sajni’ and ‘Gehra Hua’. His more recent work includes ‘Jai Jai Ram’ from the upcoming Ranbir Kapoor-starrer ‘Ramayana’, which is scheduled for a Diwali 2026 release.Diljit Dosanjh, on the other hand, has built a successful career as both a singer and an actor over the past two decades. With a strong fan base in India and overseas, he has become known for his energetic live performances and large-scale concerts. He was most recently seen in Imtiaz Ali’s ‘Main Vaapas Aaunga’, alongside Naseeruddin Shah, Sharvari and Vedang Raina.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Now Serato DJ works on your iPhone
articles.summary: Serato’s popular DJ suite is now available on mobile for the first time, including support for hardware controllers.
articles.body: Serato DJ for iOS brings the company’s pro-level DJ suite to the iPhone and iPad. Before now, the company had only dipped its toes into mobile software, with apps like Pyro that basically just added some autofades between songs in a playlist. This is the first time most of the features of its flagship DJ app have been available on a mobile device. Competitors like Rekordbox and Algoriddim have had proper mobile DJ apps for some time. If you’re a DJ used to Serato on a laptop, the workflow should feel instantly familiar. You can even transfer your library directly from Serato DJ 5.0 on your laptop to your iOS device either over USB-C or wirelessly. The mobile version supports stem separation and the company’s full suite of effects. It also includes EQ tools, BPM matching, key sync, cue points, recording, and more for live performance and capturing those performances for posterity. You can DJ directly from your touchscreen in various layouts, but Serato DJ for iOS also supports over 120 hardware controllers. With some older controllers, you might need an adapter, but it seems like compatibility with your DJ hardware shouldn’t be a major issue. It even supports Digital Vinyl Systems (DVS) for scratching and DJs who prefer the feel of real records. [Media: Serato DJ for iOS is available as a feature-limited download from the App Store. You can buy a license for $149 or get it bundled along with Serato DJ Pro, Serato Studio, and all of its expansions for $14.99 a month.

articles.title: Mariah Carey wins bitter legal battle with brother as $20M lawsuit over tell-all memoir is tossed
articles.summary: Morgan Carey's $20 million defamation lawsuit over Mariah Carey's memoir failed to satisfy the actual malice standard, a New York judge ruled.
articles.body: Mariah Carey earned a win in court after a New York judge dismissed a $20 million defamation case filed by her brother, Morgan Carey. Morgan alleged in a 2021 lawsuit that his sister's 2020 memoir, "The Meaning of Mariah Carey," contained defamatory statements and caused intentional infliction of emotional distress, according to documents obtained by Fox News Digital. In his initial complaint, Morgan wrote that Mariah's book contained "numerous passages which are of and concerning plaintiff, and which are, both individually and collectively, false and defamatory." MARIAH CAREY DIDN'T STEAL LYRICS FOR HIT SONG 'ALL I WANT FOR CHRISTMAS IS YOU,' JUDGE RULES He initially brought the action against the "We Belong Together" singer "more in sorrow and disappointment in his sister’s betrayals and malicious falsehoods than in anger at them" and claimed "the damage was intended" before press began on the book. Morgan cited a passage where the singer recalled an alleged fight between her brother and father as "false and defamatory," and claimed the excerpt alone not only portrayed him as a "physically violent man," but also fulfilled a "clichéd and racially charged portrayal of two Black males engaged in a physical struggle never happened." "It took twelve cops to pull my brother and father apart," Mariah allegedly wrote. "The big bodies of men, all entangled like a swirling hurricane, crashed loudly into the living room. I was a little girl with very few memories of a big brother who protected me." In his second amended complaint, Morgan alleged that Mariah "weaponized the death of both their parents and sister Alison," which he claimed "speaks to [Defendant's] true character, and is ample evidence of malice towards [Plaintiff.]" ALANIS MORISSETTE SUES EX-TOUR MANAGER OVER ALLEGED BLACKMAIL, FALSE DRUG TRAFFICKING CLAIMS "Having reviewed both the First and Complaints, the Court finds that Defendant did not forfeit her opportunity to above allegations in the Second Amended Complaint that were included as the Defendant's 'actual malice' necessary for Plaintiff's defamation claims," Judge Leslie A. Stroth ruled. "In the First Amended Complaint, the above instances were not alleged as being indicative of Defendant's actual malice, rather, they were largely claimed as defamatory statements themselves. The Court finds Defendant could not have responded to these instances of 'actual malice' in the First Amended Complaint, as they were not framed as such." Morgan claimed that "actual malice" was to be inferred from Mariah's "betrayal and deeply hurtful violation of [Plaintiff's] privacy" by revealing he stayed at the Sagamore Children's Psychiatric Center when he was a child, and further characterizing Morgan as "the Big Bad Wolf" in addition to her "ex-brother." "Plaintiff further states that Defendant's actual malice is also demonstrated in Defendant's Oprah Winfrey interview, and when Defendant 'weaponized' the death of the parties' parents and sister to boost commercial sales of her Memoir," documents stated. KATY PERRY FIGHTS BACK AGAINST RUBY ROSE'S 'CATEGORICALLY FALSE' SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS Morgan acknowledged in his filing that Mariah's sources for some of her "allegedly defamatory statements" are unverified, including her deceased mother, an anonymous photographer and hairstylist, in addition to "inner circle common knowledge." "The Court finds that Plaintiff has not sufficiently pleaded actual malice on the part of Defendant," the judge ruled. "Plaintiff has alleged that Defendant was more concerned with the 'commercial viability' of her Memoir, than verifying the truth of her statements, and that Defendant's sources for such statements are anonymous and/or unverifiable. BLAKE LIVELY ALLEGES ‘MEAN GIRL’ SMEAR CAMPAIGN DAMAGED HER CAREER, SEEKS UP TO $296M "Notably, Plaintiff fails to provide any proof that Defendant made such statements with knowledge of their falsity or with reckless disregard for the truth." The judge added, "While Plaintiff alleges that Defendant demonstrates ill will towards her brother, such a statement is insufficient, and Plaintiff has not satisfied the pleading requirements for actual malice in his Second Amended Complaint." WYNONNA JUDD SAYS SHE AND SISTER ASHLEY AREN'T SPEAKING AS FAMILY PAIN RESURFACES The Grammy-winning singer's familial relationships have been challenging over the years. Shortly after the release of her memoir, her sister Alison claimed Mariah intentionally inflicted "emotional distress" and filed a $1.25 million suit against the "Fantasy" singer. The suit referred to Carey as "heartless, vicious [and] vindictive," and stated that Alison had begun abusing alcohol and was "uncharacteristically tearful" after the book's release. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Carey alleged in her book that Alison gave her Valium and tried to "pimp her out" and threw boiling hot tea on her, per People, a story which Alison cited in the summons and claims "presented no evidence to substantiate." "[Carey] also callously dismisses [Alison] as her 'ex' sister," docs stated. "But instead of saying no more about her, [Carey] used her book to humiliate and embarrass plaintiff as stories about the memoir appeared in newspapers around the world, on TV and across the Internet, most of them with headlines repeating defendant's allegations — all of them published without giving [Alison] any opportunity to respond." Alison was allegedly diagnosed with PTSD, anxiety and depression, and was in therapy to process "the horrific abuse" she allegedly suffered as a child, which includes incidents she's described as "satanic" in a 2020 lawsuit against their mother, Patricia. Prior to her own suit against Mariah, Alison sued their mother, claiming she was forced to endure sexual abuse from multiple men by way of Satanic worship meetings when she was a child. Alison accused her mom, Patricia, of sexual abuse when she was 10 years old in a summons filed with the New York Supreme Court in February 2020, that was obtained by Fox News Digital at the time. Alison alleged that her mother allowed and encouraged an undisclosed number of men to engage in sexual acts such as forcible touching, sexual assault in the first degree and made her witness people engaged in sexual acts with adults and children. In her memoir, Mariah wrote that her relationship with her mother "has been full of contradictions and competing realities." A complicated love tethers my heart to my mother's," she wrote. After referring to her relationship with her mother as a "complicated love," Carey dedicated her memoir in part to Patricia. "And to Pat, my mother, who, through it all, I do believe actually did the best she could," Carey wrote. "I will love you the best I can, always." articles.title: Glastonbury Festival 2027 coach tickets oversold in admin error
articles.summary: Bookings will automatically be converted into a general admission ticket and coach fare refunded.
articles.body:
An administrative error resulted in coach journeys to the Glastonbury Festival being oversold through its official ticketing partner.

More coach package tickets were sold for certain departures than there are seats available, according to an email See Tickets sent to customers.

Those affected will not lose their tickets however. Instead, their booking will automatically be converted into a general admission ticket and the coach fare will be refunded.

The ticketing agency declined to comment further, but the BBC understands Glastonbury Festival was not responsible for the error.

Glastonbury coach ticket prices range from £26 to £185 - on top of general admission - depending on the departure town or city and whether it is a single or return journey.

'We want to give you best seat in house for Glasto'

Affected customers have been told that unless they opt to keep their coach seat by 31 October 2026, their booking will automatically be converted to general admission.

The coach fare will then be refunded to the card used for the original booking.

See Tickets' customer services department assured customers the error will not affect festival deposits, and ticket holders will be able to pay the remaining balance for their tickets as normal in April.

The agency apologised and thanked customers for their understanding, adding: "We're looking forward to welcoming you to the festival in June."

For some the news is welcome, as it provides more flexibility with travel arrangements.

Glastonbury Festival requires those who bought a coach ticket to board their designated coach for the initial journey to the festival, or entry could be denied.

It is part of the festival's Green Travel Initiatives , where they encourage revellers to use public transportation in a bid to reduce the environmental impact.

Laura Brooks, based in Birmingham, says she and her friends bought the coach package because "we had failed so often getting [general admission] tickets".

She had planned to meet them in London to travel to Somerset together, but can now arrange simpler and shorter journeys from their own respective homes.

"I don't mind the admin error, they're clearly dealing with it sooner than later. These things happen," she said.

"I'm just glad we've not lost our tickets altogether."

articles.title: Apple Music has a new logo
articles.summary: Apple Music is getting a new logo, an updated wordmark, and a new sound composed by British producer Fred Again and Nest Acoustics.
articles.body: Apple is officially launching a rebrand of Apple Music. Following the appearance of a redesigned wordmark in a video and an updated app icon in an iOS 27.2 beta, Apple introduced the new “identity” for Apple Music today. There’s a new logo, the updated wordmark, and a new sound composed by British producer Fred Again and Nest Acoustics. In a video, Apple says that for the rebrand, the company “wanted sound to create the visuals,” showing the music note logo and the wordmark underwater and how that water responded to sound. It’s a pretty cool video, honestly, and I like seeing how the water morphs the logo and wordmark. The video is also one of the most Apple things I’ve ever seen, but I still think it’s cool. The new look is expected to roll out across platforms “this week,” according to Wallpaper. I’m guessing that means it will show up in the final iOS 27.2 release, following the release candidate version of the update that launched this week.

articles.title: Supernatural’s comeback starts today, with more music and VR workouts coming soon
articles.summary: Supernatural’s new app is now available in Early Access on the Meta Horizon Store, with new VR workouts coming every week for subscribers.
articles.body: Despite Meta saying it would stop creating new content for Supernatural, the beloved fitness VR game is back after spinning off to go its own way and is relaunching with an Early Access preview in the Meta Horizon Store. Thousands of “remastered” workouts and some new ones are available in the new app starting today, but more are on the way. As previously announced, the newly independent app also costs more, going from $9.99 per month to $20 per month or $200 per year. Starting next week, Supernatural will get new workouts every week. The game’s developers also write, “More back-catalog favorites will return in the weeks and months ahead, with new music, higher-definition destinations and new features on the way.” Other new features coming later include the return of Supernatural Together, which has been “rebuilt from the ground up.” Supernatural is also getting a mobile companion app it says members can use to “Track progress and heart rate and stay connected beyond the headset.” Supernatural says people who played the original version of the game “can transfer their points, start date, streaks, favorites and badges” to the new version through December 3rd. It’s also offering rewards for “founding members,” starting with a custom bat, with more coming throughout early access.

articles.title: David Spade tells critics to ‘relax’ as Shane Gillis faces backlash over ‘SNL’ joke
articles.summary: David Spade and Dana Carvey defend Shane Gillis after his "Saturday Night Live" monologue joke about women at the gym sparked widespread backlash.
articles.body: David Spade thinks people have gotten a little too comfortable being offended. Spade defended comedians' right to push boundaries, even when their material doesn't land during an episode of his podcast, "Fly on the Wall with Dana Carvey and David Spade." Comedian Shane Gillis sparked backlash after he mocked women at the gym during his "Saturday Night Live" monologue. "I haven’t been to the gym in so long. I didn’t know women just dress like whores now?" Gillis said. "Look, I'm sorry, there's no other way to describe … Have you seen the shorts? Those neon, they're like, artificial bait-colored [shorts], and the wrinkles go around the cheeks and all combine at the butthole. And don’t look! You’re not allowed to look." JOE ROGAN DEFENDS SHANE GILLIS FROM 'WORD POLICE' AFTER SNL JOKE SPARKS LIBERAL UPROAR Carvey wasn't buying the outrage surrounding Gillis' joke. Rather than viewing the remarks as an attack on women, the comedian argued that the backlash overlooked a fundamental part of stand-up comedy: saying things that aren't meant to be taken literally. "I just didn't understand the kerfuffle," Carvey said. "Only 'cause to me, I just saw it as what we call – I'll just say it – a joke. articles.title: Hunter Schafer, actriz de 'Euphoria', revela que se ha sometido a una cirugía de afirmación de género: "Soy una mujer, soy una chica"
articles.standfirst: La intérprete ha contado en una entrevista que se operó en diciembre y que está encantada con el resultado
articles.summary: La intérprete ha contado en una entrevista que se operó en diciembre y que está encantada con el resultado
articles.body: La actriz Hunter Schafer, conocida por su papel en la serie 'Euphoria', ha revelado que se sometió a una cirugía genital de afirmación de género en diciembre. En una entrevista con la revista Elle, la intérprete ha compartido cómo vivió este proceso y cómo ha cambiado su relación con su cuerpo y su identidad. "Me sometí a una cirugía genital en diciembre de 2025, que fue increíble y me encanta", ha afirmado. La también modelo estadounidense ha explicado que durante mucho tiempo intentó aceptar su cuerpo y explorar una identidad que trascendiera las categorías tradicionales de género. "Durante mucho tiempo he aceptado la parte de mí que trasciende las categorías de género y realmente quería intentar que mi cuerpo anterior funcionara en mí, porque pensaba que había algo muy interesante y rompedor en ello", ha recordado Hunter Schafer. Sin embargo, con el tiempo comprendió que esa manera de entenderse no encajaba con cómo quería vivir y presentarse ante los demás. La intervención supuso un paso importante en ese recorrido personal, aunque la recuperación se prolongó hasta principios de 2026. Durante ese periodo, necesitó permanecer tumbada durante largos intervalos y llegó a alquilar un apartamento amplio para poder recibir las visitas de sus allegados. En la entrevista, Hunter Schafer también ha reflexionado sobre la evolución de su identidad y sobre cómo su visión del género se ha vuelto más sencilla y definida con el paso del tiempo. "Soy una mujer, soy una chica", ha afirmado al hablar sobre cómo se identifica actualmente. La activista LGBT ha descrito este recorrido como un proceso de autoconocimiento y ha defendido la importancia de poder vivir su identidad sin que esta determine por completo la percepción que los demás tienen de ella. Más allá de su experiencia personal, Hunter Schafer ha hablado de cómo quiere afrontar su futuro profesional. La intérprete ha señalado en otras ocasiones que no desea que su condición de mujer trans eclipse su trabajo como actriz ni que esta circunstancia limite los personajes que puede interpretar. "He trabajado muchísimo para llegar hasta donde estoy, después de atravesar momentos muy duros de mi transición y ahora solo quiero ser una chica y seguir adelante con eso", ha declarado. Hunter Schafer también ha reconocido que no ha recibido demasiadas propuestas para interpretar a personajes trans. Por ello, quiere que su carrera pueda desarrollarse más allá de este tipo de papeles y evitar que su identidad de género se convierta en el principal criterio a la hora de definir sus oportunidades profesionales. Conocida internacionalmente por su trabajo en 'Euphoria', en la que interpreta a Jules Vaughn, la actriz de Nueva Jersey reivindica así su derecho a decidir cómo contar su propia historia y a seguir construyendo una carrera en la que su talento interpretativo tenga un papel central.

articles.title: Zach Bryan admits he drank '15 beers a day' as part of 'perfect routine' before quitting alcohol
articles.summary: Zach Bryan told Matthew McConaughey he drank up to 15 beers a day and was drunk when he wrote nearly every hit before a pivotal moment changed him.
articles.body: Zach Bryan is getting candid about his relationship with alcohol, revealing that he once drank as many as 15 beers a day and was intoxicated when he wrote nearly every hit song of his career. The country star, 30, opened up about his sobriety during a conversation with Matthew McConaughey that was released alongside his latest EP, "Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs." Bryan detailed how his drinking eventually led to severe panic attacks that left him fearing he was going to die. ZACH BRYAN ADMITS QUICK RISE TO FAME AFTER DECADE OF MILITARY SERVICE LED TO ALCOHOL DEPENDENCY "When I got in the throes of drinking f---ing 15 beers in a day and I kept going with that cycle, I started getting these really, really severe panic attacks where my whole body went numb, and I thought I was going to have a stroke and die," he told McConaughey. "I’d curl up for days at a time, and I went to a doctor. And, like I said, I still didn’t believe it. I told the doctor, ‘Man, I’m just hungover. I’m fine.’ And the doctor was like, ‘No, man. You have a really severe thing going on here.’" Bryan said his doctor diagnosed him with panic disorder and suggested that quitting alcohol could help. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "[My doctor] said, ‘I think you have a pretty bad panic disorder. And if you quit drinking, that might help you a little bit.’ So I tried it, and I was like, ‘Oh, yeah.’" Before giving up alcohol, Bryan said he relied on drinking to manage his stage fright. "So I used to get on stage. Here’s my routine. I used to think this was the perfect routine. No show could ever go bad if I did this: work out, shower, play my guitar, listen to Bon Iver, drink four beers," he recalled. "It eased my pain. All the stage fright I had was gone after I drank three or four beers, and I’m like, ‘I can do it.’ Then I would drink after the show, too." Bryan said he would wake up the next day facing another performance and repeat the same cycle. "I’d wake up the next day with another show, and I’d think, ‘Well, to get rid of this panic in me, to get rid of this stage fright, there’s one choice. Let’s do what we’ve always done,’" he said. "I’d drink two or three more beers. And I thought I was never going to get out of that. I thought that cycle was forever." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS The singer-songwriter said his managers had questioned whether he had tried performing without alcohol, but he viewed drinking as part of his routine. "They would always be like, ‘Hey, have you tried not drinking before a show?’ Like, I can’t. It’s my routine. It’s my lucky socks," Bryan said. "For a long time, I danced with that. Years, I danced with that. And it worked, you know. I was playing a good show. I was paying my bills. I was doing everything. I employed 100 or 200 people. I was like, ‘This is fine.’" Bryan said performing sober is more intimidating at first, but ultimately more rewarding. "I will say now that I’ve quit drinking, stages are more scary," he admitted. "But once I get on stage, it’s a lot more enjoyable. So much better. It feels like flying. It’s more fun. It’s the best feeling in the world." Bryan said the realization that he was responsible for his own struggles came after years of denial. "I used to be so terrified of that," he said of performing sober. "And that denial is what got me there. That denial is what brought me to those panic attacks. I was the issue the whole time." The Grammy winner also said he had convinced himself that alcohol was essential to his songwriting process. "Every hit I ever had, I was pretty much drunk when I made it," Bryan said. "And so I had the issue of thinking I was never going to have a good song again if I wasn’t under the influence." He described the belief as a "real curse" that made him feel as though he had to repeat the same rituals in order to create music. "This is the first project I’ve ever done, this ‘Young Manhood’ thing, that I didn’t drink a lick," he said. "I wrote every word sober and I sang every word sober. And I’ll say it took that to prove to me that I could do it." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Bryan admitted that he once dismissed sobriety and didn't recognize that his own drinking had become a problem. "I always thought sobriety was a joke because it’s people who couldn’t control themselves celebrating not being able to control themselves," Bryan said. "When I was drinking a lot, I always thought, ‘Why can’t you control yourself?’ I never realized I had a problem." The singer said his perspective changed during a solo 30-day motorcycle trip across the country. Bryan said he spent much of the trip stopping at bars and drinking himself to sleep. When he reached a Pilot truck stop outside Seattle, he bought a 40-ounce Budweiser and sat on a curb beside his motorcycle. "I’ll never forget this as long as I live," he said. "I went into this Pilot and I grabbed a 40 [ounce bottle of] Budweiser, and I’m sitting on the curb with my motorcycle in front of me, and I’m drinking it. And I’m thinking, ‘What the hell was all that worth? Why did I do any of that? I feel emptier than when I left.’" Bryan said he realized he had spent the previous 30 days chasing a "big romantic movie moment," only to find himself alone in a parking lot. "I’ve got nowhere to go home to, no one to call," he recalled thinking. "That’s when I said, ‘Man, why am I drinking right now? What am I celebrating?’" "It changed me a lot, that parking lot," he said. "That was the moment I realized, when I went and got that 40, I was like, ‘Man, it’s f---ing 3. You’ve got an issue. Why do you want to drink a 40 right now in the Seattle Pilot parking lot?’" Bryan previously announced in November 2025 that he had been sober for two months, writing that he had used alcohol to cope with a "perpetual discontent" and a "consistent black hole" inside him. articles.title: Taylor Swift wasn’t pleased when Jason Kelce woke her and Travis Kelce at 7:30 am to ask his brother to spot him during a workout: ‘This is f---ed up’
articles.summary: Taylor Swift was not particularly pleased when Jason Kelce woke her and Travis Kelce up early in the morning with a workout-related request.
articles.body: Taylor Swift was not particularly pleased when Jason Kelce woke her and Travis Kelce up early in the morning with a workout-related request. The retired NFL star had called his younger brother at 7:30 am, leaving Travis worried that something had gone wrong, only to discover that Jason wanted him to help with a gym session.The amusing incident came up during the Wednesday, October 21, episode of the brothers’ New Heights podcast, where they discussed Jason’s participation in the fitness challenge ‘Squatober’. While Travis was more than willing to help his brother, Swift apparently found the timing and circumstances less amusing.Jason Kelce’s unusual trip to Kansas City for SquatoberTravis revealed that Jason had asked him about the weights he kept in his basement before travelling to Kansas City, Missouri, with additional equipment for his workout.“I knew Jason was doing Squatober,” Travis said, recalling how his older brother had asked him how much weight he had at home. Jason eventually arrived with two 25-pound weights to add to his workout setup.“A couple extra plates to throw on the old squat bar,” Travis joked, calling it “the most meathead thing I think I’ve ever seen Jason do”.But Jason’s dedication to fitness soon led to an early morning interruption that Travis was not expecting.Travis Kelce feared something had gone wrongTravis said he was alarmed when his phone rang at 7:30 am. Still half-asleep, the Chiefs tight end immediately imagined that his brother might have suffered an injury.“I get a call at 7:30 in the morning. In my mind, I’m thinking worst-case scenario,” Travis recalled. He wondered whether Jason had hurt himself during a run or blown out his knee while exercising.Instead, Jason was perfectly fine and had called for a favour.“Jason’s like, ‘Yeah, can you come spot me?’ I was just like, ‘No way!’” Travis said, laughing as he recounted his brother’s request.Jason then clarified that he was doing bench presses rather than squats. Travis admitted that the news came as a relief because he would not have been able to save his brother if he had been attempting a heavy back squat.“I got my ankle wrap. And he’s like, ‘Nah, nah, it’s bench, it’s bench. It’s not squat.’ And I’m like, cool, ‘cause I wouldn’t be able to save you if it was a f---ing back squat. I’m like, ‘Cool, I’ll come down,’” Travis said.What Taylor Swift said when Travis agreed to helpAlthough Travis was ready to head down and spot Jason during his workout, Swift was apparently unimpressed by the situation.Travis recalled that as he was leaving the room, the pop star reacted to the early morning call by saying, “This is f---ed up.”Her response prompted laughter from the brothers, particularly as Travis remained determined to help Jason.“And I’m just like, ‘Nah, it’ll be good. It’ll be good!’” Travis added.The exchange highlighted the easygoing dynamic between the brothers, even as Jason’s gym plans unexpectedly brought Swift into the conversation. While Travis saw no problem with helping his older brother, Swift’s reaction suggested that a 7:30 am workout request was hardly an ideal way to start the day.Jason Kelce and Taylor Swift cheer for Travis at Arrowhead StadiumThe brothers also spoke about being together at Arrowhead Stadium over the weekend, where the Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Los Angeles Chargers.Jason confirmed that he attended a New Heights tailgate ahead of the game.
